title: Animations that feel right
sourceNote: animate, review-animations and improve-animations skills, MIT licence
summary: Decide whether to animate, then pick the cheapest tool, the right curve and a short duration.

overview.purpose: Build, review and audit UI motion so it feels quick, purposeful and interruptible.
overview.when: Adding motion to a component, reviewing an animation diff, or auditing a whole codebase.
takeaways: Name the purpose before you build
Reduced motion ships with the animation

sections.title: Should it animate?
sections.intro: Two gates run before any curve or duration.

items.title: 100+ times a day
items.more: Keyboard shortcuts and command-palette toggles open instantly. Raycast has no open animation, and that is correct.

items.title: Tens of times a day
items.more: Hover effects and list navigation: fast and subtle, or instant.

items.title: Name the purpose
items.text: Feedback, spatial, state, bridge, explain, delight.
items.more: If you cannot name one, do not build it. Data the user is reading should not move for style.

sections.title: Tool and properties
sections.intro: Cheapest tool that works; GPU properties only.

items.title: CSS transition
items.more: Transitions retarget from the current value, so they stay interruptible.

items.title: @starting-style
items.more: Lets a freshly inserted element transition from a start state.
items.css:
.toast { transition: opacity 200ms, transform 200ms; }
@starting-style { .toast { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px); } }

items.title: Web Animations API
transform and opacity
items.more: Height is tolerated only for accordions. Never transition: all.

items.title: Never scale(0)
items.more: Nothing in the real world appears from nothing.

items.title: Origin at the trigger
items.more: Modals are exempt and stay centred.

sections.title: Curves and duration
sections.intro: Built-in easings are too weak. Use strong curves and short durations.

items.title: Strong ease-out
items.more: The default. ease-out at 200 ms feels faster than ease-in at 200 ms.

items.title: Strong ease-in-out
items.more: For elements that travel or morph while visible.

items.title: Never ease-in on UI
items.text: It delays the moment you watch.
items.more: ease-in starts slow, exactly when the user is looking.

items.title: Durations
items.more: Tooltips 125–200 ms, modals and drawers 200–500 ms. UI stays under 300 ms unless there is a reason.

items.title: Springs for gestures
items.more: Keep bounce at 0.1–0.3 and avoid it in most UI.

sections.title: Review standards
sections.intro: Flag on sight when reviewing motion.
items: Animation on a keyboard shortcut or 100+/day action
UI duration over 300 ms with no reason
Animating width, height, margin, top or left
Everything entering at once (use a 30–80 ms stagger)
